THREE INSTRUCTIONS TO ACT ON AT THE OPEN, ALL ON MONEY ALREADY AT RISK, AND NONE OF THEM IS A NEW POSITION. Ranking puts them at 5, 6 and 7 because the ranking rule is conviction-then-reward-to-risk, so read them here first: (1) HII, rank 5 — a +19.7% gain is carrying NO STOP; trim half at market 313-315 and place a 235.00 stop on the remainder. A fourth, ACM at rank 4, is dated rather than immediate: be trimmed by the close on Monday 2026-11-16.

WHAT THIS REPORT IS. Research ran 06:00:52-06:33 ET and was NOT truncated — notes.md carries a RESEARCH COMPLETE block and the work finished inside its budget. Of the seven ideas that survive the red team, SIX are position management rather than new opportunities: ACM, KHC, HII and PFE are hold/trim/accumulate decisions on open positions, and AAL and BCC are close instructions. HUN was published as an unchanged re-pitch of the 2026-11-10 level at 9.00 and the red team CUT it — the levels were not in fact unchanged; see the red-team note at the end of this field. EXACTLY ONE IDEA IS NEW: ADM at rank 3. Size the page accordingly; seven rows is not seven fresh opportunities.

WHY ONLY ONE NEW IDEA. Not a thin research day — it is what the tape offered, and the rejections are specific. The market is split in two with no middle. The leaders are 1-5% off their 120-day highs, so a properly wide 2.0-ATR stop puts every 2:1 target ABOVE the range high (XLV, LOW, HD, DIS, WMT, BJ and TGT were all rejected for exactly this, with the arithmetic shown for XLV and TGT). The names with room are below falling moving averages with no support to anchor a stop (AMAT -49.6% in 120 days, CSCO, KEYS, PANW). TJX had clean geometry and was rejected on evidence: $27.7M of insider sales, zero buys, revisions -6.8pp. C and KEY were rejected despite improving revisions and four straight beats each. The one screen that found anything was revision direction, and it surfaced HUN (+23.8pp) and ADM (+22.8pp), both deeply de-rated cyclicals at their lows.

NVDA IS ABSENT ON PURPOSE. Its 166.00 stop was touched on 2026-11-10 — the bar low was 165.89 — so the position opened 2026-11-07 at 184.00 is already closed at roughly -9.8%, and a closed position cannot be amended. A fresh NVDA long into the 11-17 print was considered and rejected: 1.8% off a 90-day low with no support beneath it, where a 2.0-ATR stop sits near 150 and no defensible target gives 2:1. The de-rating is sectoral, not company-specific — semis have shed $3.3 trillion since June 22 and SMH is -18.17% over one month.

RATIOS SITTING ON THE FLOOR — read this before sizing. Three of the six swing ideas clear their 2.0 reward-to-risk floor with almost no margin: ACM 2.0000, HUN 2.0000 and ADM 2.0909. That clustering is the signature the pipeline exists to catch, so here is what the recomputation found. All three were recomputed from entry, stop and target independently of the figures in the notes, and every one matched; ACM and HUN land at 2.0 exactly, not nudged above it. ADM was explicitly corrected during research's own falsification pass: as first captured at entry 69.20 it computed to exactly 2.00 and could have failed validation on floating point, and the fix taken was to move the ENTRY down onto the real level — 68.80 is the 120-day low of 68.793 itself — leaving the target untouched, rather than tightening the stop or lifting the target. Stop distances were verified in ATRs against the live atr14: ACM 2.46, KHC 2.29, HII 2.01, HUN 2.19, ADM 2.10, all clearing the 2.0 swing floor. No ratio here was bought with a tight stop.

TARGETS AT THE RANGE HIGH — the structural caveat on this whole book. Three of the published ideas carry a target at or above the instrument's own 120-day high: ACM 77.22 against a 76.85 high, HII 339.76 against 334.53, and KHC 28.09 which IS the range high to the cent. Those targets are inherited from the original publications and were deliberately not revised, but they mean the trade needs a breakout to pay out while the stop only needs an ordinary pullback. Research found the same pattern across seven of the fourteen open positions, plus four live stops tighter than the ATR floor now enforced (UNP 1.39 ATR, PYPL 1.42, ABT 1.97, XLE 1.64 against a 1.8 ETF floor). That combination is a mechanical explanation for the 10% hit rate that requires none of the theses to have been wrong, and it may be the most useful output today. The sub-floor stops were flagged, not widened — walking a live stop is the mirror image of the abuse the floor exists to stop.

FOUR DELIBERATE VALIDATION FAILURES — do not repair these, they are the message. (1) AAL's stop is 1.61 ATR from entry, under the 2.0 swing floor. It was under the floor the day it was published and is inherited, not newly set; the stop on a position being closed is not being widened. (2) AAL's win_probability is 0.15 against a 0.276 break-even baseline, which makes expectancy negative and should fail enforcement. That is the machine-readable way to say this position no longer has an edge, not a number to fix. (3) BCC's reward-to-risk is 2.31 against the 2.5 long_term floor, priced against an honest 62.00 bear case below the 65.41 range low — the fact that it would not clear the bar as a new idea today IS the argument for closing it. (4) AAL at conviction 2 (two evidence kinds) and BCC at conviction 2 (three kinds) are both scored BELOW what the kind count mechanically supports, because in both the evidence argues for the EXIT rather than for the position, and counting evidence-against as conviction-for would invert the score. Do not raise them. If enforcement demotes AAL or BCC to the watchlist, the close instructions above still stand — that is why they are restated at the top of this field.

SOURCES THAT FAILED, AND THE THREE LANES LOST TO THEM. Index levels and VIX are UNAVAILABLE: Yahoo returned HTTP 429 for ^GSPC, ^NDX, ^DJI, ^RUT and ^VIX, finnhub paywalls CFD indices, stooq 404s on ^-prefixed symbols and there is no alphavantage key. CRYPTO HISTORY: history BTC-USD returns ok:false, so no ATR, so no crypto or crypto-futures idea was published — including the /MBTZ6 short sitting in awaiting-entry at 74,075 with BTC spot at 73,930, a live level with a supportive macro read, withheld because a futures idea without a stop is not publishable. Spot crypto quotes via coingecko do work. All three lanes were lost to data sources, not to judgement. Nothing intraday cleared the bar and nothing intraday was manufactured.

PRICES AND SESSION. Every price in this report except one is the 2026-11-10 16:00 ET close, re-quoted at 06:30 ET and unchanged — that is a closed market, not stale data, and at 06:30 ET the previous close is the freshest honest equity price. The exception is ADM, whose 69.61 is a live pre-market quote from nasdaq depth at 06:20 ET with a 0.187% bid-ask spread; the 06:30 finnhub re-quote returned the 69.30 prior close, which is older, so the pre-market print was kept. All rates are dated and will not refresh: 10y 4.88% and 2y 4.56% are FRED reads dated 2026-11-09, the 0.25 curve is dated 2026-11-10.

TODAY IS VETERANS DAY. Equities trade regular hours 09:30-16:00 ET — it is not an NYSE holiday — but SIFMA recommends a full close of the US fixed income market and the Federal Reserve Banks are closed. Three consequences: no economic releases and no FRED refresh today; TLT will trade on flow with no cash-bond price discovery, which is an independent second reason not to enter the 80.30 TLT level on top of the macro one; and volumes are typically thin on a partial holiday, which argues against initiating at the open and in favour of the limit entries every idea here uses.

Counting published ideas plus positions held unchanged, healthcare is AT the 3-idea cap (PFE published, ABT and SMMT held), which is a second reason XLV was rejected beyond its geometry. Defence is 2 and falls to roughly 1.5 on the HII trim. KHC and ADM are counted as two drivers — branded packaged-food volumes versus agricultural processing and crush margins — and that is a judgement call rather than a fact: a reader who thinks food is food should treat them as one 4.5% position rather than two. Either way it is under the cap. One more disclosure on consistency: ADM is a purchase at a 120-day low below falling moving averages, which is the shape AMAT and CSCO were rejected for this morning. The distinction research drew is that those two have a binary print tomorrow and 6.93% and 3.98% daily ATRs, whereas ADM has already reported, has no print inside the window, runs a 3.03% ATR and has beaten consensus four quarters running. That is still a bet against six months of price, which is why conviction is 3 and size is 2%.

TRACK RECORD CONTEXT, NOT ACTED ON. The record is 4/39 at target (10%), avg -5.9%. Conviction 3 is the worst bucket with a real sample at 2/25 (8%), avg -6.9% over 25 closed trades, which is past the ~15 noise threshold — so the four conviction-3 ideas here were each held to a higher bar, and TJX was rejected partly on that basis. The long_term bucket is 0/4, avg -15.2%, but four closed trades is well under the noise threshold, so it is noted rather than acted on against PFE.

RED TEAM (phase 2c). One cut, two conviction downgrades, five disclosures, and one pipeline defect that will mis-handle this report at phase 2d. Every level in all eight ideas was reverified against market_data.py history and every one matched to the stated decimal (ranges, SMA20/50, ATR14 for ACM, PFE, HII, KHC, ADM, HUN and BCC), and all eight reward-to-risk ratios recompute from their own entry, target and stop. The arithmetic on this report is clean; the problems are elsewhere.

CUT: HUN. The 2.0000:1 was solved for. It was published yesterday at 9.00/10.82/8.09 for exactly 2.0000:1 on a stop of 2.003 ATR; ATR14 ticked from 0.4543 to 0.4572 overnight, which puts that same stop at 1.990 ATR, under the 2.0 swing floor. The stop was correctly widened to 8.00 (2.19 ATR) and the target was walked from 10.82 to a round 11.00 in the same stroke, restoring exactly 2.0000:1 — while the scale_plan asserted the level was UNCHANGED and that nothing had changed in a session. On the properly floored stop and the target actually in force the idea is 1.82:1, and the only structural level named anywhere in it (10.40, the pre-de-rating SMA50) gives 1.40:1. Nothing anchors 11.00. A ratio pinned to the floor to four decimals across two different level pairs is the exact artifact phases 2b-2d exist to catch, and it was wearing a label saying no level had moved. Full reasoning is on the watchlist entry.

THE FINDING THAT APPLIES TO FOUR MORE ROWS: a published reward-to-risk is measured from the entry, and on a position update the entry is a fill the market has left behind. Nobody can transact these ratios. HII publishes 2.88:1 and offers 0.33:1 from 313.57 (26.19 of reward against 78.57 of risk to the stop being placed today). ACM publishes 2.00:1 and offers 0.72:1 from 70.63. KHC publishes 2.83:1 and offers 1.27:1 from 24.24, under the swing floor. PFE publishes 4.00:1 and offers 2.36:1 at 29.36, under the 2.5 long_term floor — which is a reason not to add at the market, though the plan's sub-28.00 and sub-26.00 adds clear it at 3.5:1 and 8.0:1 and so stand. ADM is the only surviving row whose entry is still in front of the market, and therefore the only one whose ratio is live. None of this is a fabrication and no level was moved to fix it: the trim and hold instructions are correct, it is the numbers beside them that are stale, and the from-here arithmetic is now written into each idea's counter_argument. This compounds the report's own 'targets at the range high' caveat, because a target above the high is exactly how a filled winner ends up with all of its ratio behind it.

DOWNGRADES. HII 3 -> 2, size 2.0% -> 1.0%, tier standard -> speculative: both of its evidence items argue against holding (5.6M USD of insider sales with zero buys, -4.05% 3m and -5.99% 6m relative, target above the range high), and the validator counts evidence kinds without regard to their direction. This report applied the right rule to AAL and BCC and then did not apply it to HII. ACM 4 -> 3: its dated_catalyst is a date that is not company-confirmed, with three sources disagreeing on the day and the session, which is not a clean confirmation but the reason the instruction had to straddle both. In both cases state/open_positions.json already carries the lower score (HII 2 at 1%, ACM 3), so the published figures would have recorded an UPGRADE on the morning each position is being cut — conviction and size are amended into state by apply_amendment, so this was not cosmetic. PFE kept at 4, KHC and ADM kept at 3; ADM in particular is the cleanest geometry in the book and the only ratio bought the right way, by moving the entry down onto the measured 68.793 low.

AAL AND BCC LEFT EXACTLY AS WRITTEN, deliberately. Their validation failures are the message and were not repaired: AAL's 1.61 ATR stop is inherited and a stop on a position being closed is not widened, and its 0.15 win probability against a 0.276 baseline is the machine-readable statement that the edge is gone. BCC's 2.31:1 against the 2.5 long_term floor is the argument for closing. Both will be demoted by phase 2d and both should be. One thing the report does not say: a close has no machine representation here. positions_from_report carries entry, target and stop but not time_stop, so setting time_stop to 2026-11-11 on AAL and BCC does nothing to state/open_positions.json — AAL stays open with its 14.40 stop and BCC stays open with no stop until a human acts or grading closes them. The CLOSE AT MARKET instructions at the top of this field are the whole mechanism. The same gap works against HII in the other direction: the 235.00 stop reaches state only via the recommendation row, so if phase 2d demotes HII the stop is never recorded and a +19.7% position stays unprotected in the tracker.

PIPELINE DEFECT, NOT A FINDING ABOUT ANY IDEA — read before trusting phase 2d. Four ideas carry a FAILING spread check taken from a pre-market book at 06:37 ET: ACM 12.22% (bid 64.15 / ask 72.50 on a name doing 92M USD a day), HII 11.97% (304.01 / 342.70 on 187M a day), BCC 7.14% (67.50 / 72.50) and HUN 21.50% (29M a day). market_data.quote_depth documents itself as returning no bid/ask outside regular hours, and that is the behaviour check_spread was written against — its no-depth branch is a WARN reading 'normal outside regular hours'. Nasdaq is in fact serving an indicative pre-market book, check_spread has no session guard, and the 4.0% fail threshold is a regular-hours threshold. Yesterday's 06:37 run quoted ACM at 1.839% and NVDA at 0.039%, so this is a thin Veterans Day pre-market book being measured as though the market were open, not a tradability fact. Consequence: phase 2d will demote ACM, HII and BCC on an artifact (AAL and BCC also fail on real grounds), and with HII goes the only route by which its 235.00 stop reaches the tracker. HUN at 1.67B cap and 29M a day is the one name where a wide spread is plausibly real, and it has been cut on other grounds. The fix belongs in validate_report.py — skip or warn rather than fail the spread check when market_session is not 'regular' — and is not applied here, because changing validation logic to save ideas from validation is the wrong move for a red team to make mid-run.

CORRELATION, BEYOND THE SECTOR CAPS THE REPORT ALREADY DISCLOSES. The sector caps are respected, but they are not what concentrates this book. PFE, KHC, ADM and the cut HUN are one signal expressed four times: a de-rated name, a six-month relative-return deficit, one open-market insider purchase, and a sell-side revision count — all long, all betting the rotation out of long-duration growth keeps running into deep value. If insider-buy-plus-revisions is a weak signal it is weak in all of them at once, which is the shape a 2-of-25 record in the conviction-3 bucket would take. Three of the four are already small (2.0-2.5%) and the fourth is cut, so no further reduction is imposed; it is named here because the report counted drivers by sector and this one crosses sectors.

RANKING. Renumbered 1-7 on the stated conviction-then-reward-to-risk convention after the downgrades: PFE 1, KHC 2, ADM 3, ACM 4, HII 5, AAL 6, BCC 7. The convention was kept rather than re-ordered by urgency so that a reader who knows the rule is not misled, which means the three act-at-the-open instructions still sit at 5, 6 and 7 and the restatement at the top of this field is still how they get delivered. The rank references in the paragraphs above have been updated to match. Validation demoted 4 idea(s) whose numbers did not check out. 3 more carry warnings — see the validation block on each.

market_context.summary: One coherent macro trade, not noise: real rates repricing higher and the market taking out Fed cuts. On 2026-11-10 yields rose at the short end, the dollar gained (+0.62%), gold fell hard (-2.68%) and long-duration tech fell (XLK -1.15%, SMH -0.78%) while financials (+0.52%), healthcare (+0.29%), energy (+0.44%) and staples (+0.15%) rose. The 10y-2y curve flattened to 0.25 from 0.32 in a day. Underneath the session sits a six-month rotation that is the dominant fact: SMH -18.17% over one month and -13.83% over six, XLK -13.98% over one month, against XLV +29.50% over six months and XLF +13.01%, with SPY +1.59% over six. Semiconductors have shed $3.3 trillion in market value since June 22. Everything long-duration — growth multiples, gold, TLT, utilities — is on the wrong side of it, which mechanically raises the bar for the TLT and XLU exposure in the book and lowers it for financials. The resulting problem for idea generation is that the tape has no middle: the leaders sit 1-5% off their highs with no room for a 2:1 target above a properly wide stop, and the names with room sit below falling moving averages with no support to anchor one. Index levels and VIX are unavailable this run, so the tape is proxied by ETF closes. Today is Veterans Day: equities trade regular hours, the cash bond market is closed, and there are no economic releases.

recommendations.thesis: Continuing position opened 2026-08-18 at 27.60, now 29.36, being carried rather than re-opened. The claim is a multiple, not a catalyst: summing the four fetched quarterly actuals (0.87, 0.77, 0.75, 0.66) gives 3.05 of trailing EPS, so at 29.36 Pfizer trades on 9.6 times trailing earnings while beating consensus every one of those four quarters by 17.6%, 11.4%, 3.5% and 14.3%. A business that has beaten four consecutive prints is not being valued like one. Insiders agree with the arithmetic: three distinct officers and directors bought 2,960,110 dollars of stock on the open market in August, led by CEO Albert Bourla at 26.34. And it is in the leadership sector — XLV is +29.50% over six months against SPY +1.59%.
recommendations.key_risk: INVALIDATION CONDITION, since this carries no stop by design: close the position if trailing four-quarter EPS falls below 2.40, or if Pfizer misses consensus on two consecutive quarters. Either would mean the patent-cliff erosion is outrunning the pipeline and the 9.6x multiple is correct rather than cheap, which is the whole bear case. A price decline alone is not invalidation and is expected during accumulation. Note also that the long_term bucket in this report is 0 of 4 at target, avg -15.2% — but that is 4 closed trades, far under the ~15 needed to be signal, so it is noted rather than acted on.
recommendations.counter_argument: The strongest case against is that the 42.00 target needs the multiple to expand from 9.6x to 13.8x trailing, and big pharma has spent years refusing to re-rate on exactly these arguments — a cheap stock that stays cheap is the base case, not a bug. Two things answer it rather than assert it away: the de-rating is no longer happening, since PFE outperforms SPY on all three windows measured (+3.38% 1m, +11.59% 3m, +13.49% 6m), and the bear case is priced at 24.00 — roughly the 23.62 120-day low — which still leaves 4.0 reward-to-risk against the 2.5 long_term floor. Sell-side bullish share is only 38.2% and slightly deteriorating, which is the setup, not the refutation. RED TEAM: conviction 4 and the 42.00 target survive — the arithmetic was recomputed independently and holds (0.87+0.77+0.75+0.66 = 3.05, 29.36/3.05 = 9.6x, 42.00 = 13.8x, 24.00 = 7.9x, and the quarterly actuals rise chronologically 0.66 -> 0.75 -> 0.77 -> 0.87 rather than erode, which is what the melting-ice-cube bear case needs and does not have). Two specifics the page was missing. First, the 4.0:1 is measured off the 27.60 fill from August: at the live 29.36 the ratio to a 24.00 bear case is 2.36:1, which is BELOW the 2.5 floor a long_term idea must clear. The accumulation plan is unaffected because it buys under 28.00 (3.5:1) and under 26.00 (8.0:1) — but do not add at 29.36, where this idea would not be publishable as new. Second, the positioning evidence is August 2026 insider buying, cited at the time this position was opened in August; three months on it is the original case being carried, not a fresh confirmation, and the one genuinely new item is relative strength, the weakest kind here. Price is also below its own SMA20 of 29.85, which the technical_level evidence omits by citing only the rising SMA50 at 28.79.

recommendations.thesis: ADM closed 69.30 on 2026-11-10, which is 0.74% off its 120-day low of 68.793 and 21.9% below its 88.75 high, and the operating business does not explain that. It has beaten consensus four quarters running — 1.77 vs 1.619 for the quarter ended 2026-09-30 (+9.3%), 1.84 vs 1.451 (+26.8%), 0.71 vs 0.666 (+6.6%) and 0.87 vs 0.804 (+8.2%). Two independent parties have acted on the gap in the last week: David R McAtee II bought 2,800 shares on the open market at 70.27 on 2026-11-05, the only insider transaction in six months in either direction, and the sell side has moved bullish share +22.8 points to 33.3%, the second-largest improvement found in any name screened today. Agricultural processing is also a genuinely separate driver from everything else in this book.
recommendations.key_risk: This is a purchase at the 120-day low below a SMA20 of 76.69 and a SMA50 of 80.61 that are both falling, with ADM lagging SPY on every window measured (-13.83% 1m, -13.08% 3m, -14.16% 6m). There is no support beneath the 68.793 low to point at, which is why the stop sits 6.4% below it rather than just under it, and why size is 2% rather than standard. Reward-to-risk is 2.09, close to the floor: this idea has little margin for an adverse detail and should be the first cut if the red team needs to cut one.
recommendations.counter_argument: The strongest case against is that this is the same falling-knife shape I rejected AMAT and CSCO for this morning, and consistency should reject it too. The distinction is specific rather than convenient: those two have a binary earnings print tomorrow inside a sector that has lost 3.3 trillion dollars of value since June and daily ATRs of 6.93% and 3.98%, whereas ADM has already reported, has no print inside the window, runs a 3.03% ATR, and has beaten four times in a row. The thing falling in semis is the demand estimate; the thing falling in ADM is the multiple on earnings that keep coming in ahead. That is still a bet against six months of price, which is why conviction is 3 and size is 2%. RED TEAM: kept at conviction 3, size 2%, levels untouched — this is the only idea in the report whose published ratio is one you can still transact at, since the 68.80 entry is 0.7% below the market rather than a fill left behind by a move, and every level was reverified against source (range low 68.793, SMA20 76.6915, SMA50 80.6146, ATR14 2.0998, all exact). The 2.09:1 is the honest floor-clearing case, not the solved-for one: the entry was moved DOWN onto the measured low rather than the target out or the stop in. One overstatement corrected. The thesis says 'two independent parties have acted on the gap in the last week'; one of the two is a change in sell-side bullish share, which is not a party acting on anything and is the same sell side this report treats as a lagging indicator elsewhere. The positioning evidence is one open-market purchase of 196,756 USD by a director — real, and the only insider transaction in six months in either direction, but director-sized, not the 5.0M USD CEO conviction cited for KHC. And the revision improvement is +22.8pp to 33.3%, so two thirds of the sell side remains un-bullish. Conviction 3 and 2% size are the right home for that; 4 would not have been.

Entry 9.00 with the properly floored 8.00 stop and the target that was actually in force gives 1.82:1, under the floor; the only structural level named anywhere in the idea is 10.40, the pre-de-rating SMA50, which gives 1.40:1. A ratio pinned to the floor to four decimal places across two different level pairs is the signature this phase exists to catch. Separately, `catalyst.wait` flipped from false to true, which would have stopped the new levels from ever reaching the tracker: positions_from_report skips waiting ideas, so state/open_positions.json would have kept grading HUN against 8.09/10.82 while the report showed 8.00/11.00. Huntsman bought 100,000 shares at 9.81 on 2026-08-03, the only insider transaction in six months, and bullish share has improved +23.8pp — but it improved to 33.3%, so two thirds of the sell side is still not bullish, the company missed three of its last four prints (0.04 vs 0.07 Sep-26, 0.00 vs 0.054 Jun-26), and the idea's own key_risk names a secondary offering as how the thesis dies.
